full_judgment: 9. Mr. Md. Jahangir Kabir, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that the RS and the SA Khatians in respect of 1(one) decimal land in Plot No. 454/ 835 has been recorded in the name of Koram Ali, predecessor of the defendants and the plaintiff could not rebut the correctness of the said Khatian, but the learned appellate Court without reversing those findings allowed the appeal thus committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that the learned trial Court found that the record of suit land does not stand in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff in the RS and the SA Khatian and as such, the heirs of Nur Banu and Jeil Banu had no right to sell the suit land in favour of the plaintiff, but the appellate Court in allowing the appeal committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that in view of the findings that there are defects in the deeds (exhibit nos.4 and 5) of the plaintiff in spite of that the appellate Court committed an error of law by allowing the appeal. He further submits that the trial Court found that PW1 stated in his cross-examination that the name of deed giver of the plaintiff was not recorded in the RS and the SA record and PW3 stated in his cross-examination that the father of defendant No.18 is the owner of the studio and PW4 stated in his cross-examination that they did not file any suit against uncorrected record, but the appellate Court below by allowing the appeal committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that defendant. Nos.18-20 along with 17(ka) to 17(Ja) obtained this suit land through inheritance and they are still in possession on the suit land and earlier the predecessor of the said defendants obtained the suit land through settlement (pattan) from earlier owner and the name of the predecessor of the said defendants was recorded in the SA and the RS Khatians correctly and the said defendants are still in possession of the suit land and the plaintiff has no possession in the suit land, but the appellate Court below committed an error of law. He further submits that the trial Court found that as per SA Khatian Nos.103 and 83, the said SA record was made in the names of the father of defendant Nos.18- 20 along with the name of dead defendant No.17 in respect of the suit land; that the said defendant mainly claimed that the land under earlier Plot No. 415/647 and the plaintiff claimed land Hal Plot No.454/647 are not same land. On the other hand, the plaintiff claimed that both the land under those plots are same, but in respect of this, the plaintiff did not prove the same through any Advocate Commissioner and the plaintiff did not also prove the same through filing the plot Index in respect of the suit land, but the Court of appeal below committed an error of law by allowing the appeal. He further submits that the trial Court found that the plaintiff's alleged deeds were made as per RS and SA record, but wherein the names of the deed given is absent, so the said alleged deeds are illegal and ineffective. He further submits that the SA and the RS records were prepared in the name of Koram Ali in respect of the suit land who was the father of defendants Nos.18-20. The rent of the suit land was paid by said Koram Ali till 1418 to 1419 B.S. dated 14.06.2013 and subsequently, the said rent of the suit land was paid by defendant No.18, Nurul Islam till 1425 BS dated 23.01.2018 and defendant Nos.18-20 are the successors of said Karam Ali, whose name was recorded in SA and RS record properly and as per pattan, SA and RS records along with plot Index, the instant petitioners are bona fide owners and possessors of the suit land. He further submits that the High Court Division considered some citations regarding question of limitation. He further submits that the judgment and decree suffers from gross illegality and legal infirmity and as such, the same is not sustainable in law and liable to be set aside.
